messages.subject: Re: Issue with estimate profiles
parts:
Steve, sure thing, any time –

 

  • The functions that use MPlus (those that end in _mplus) use random starts; see estimate_profiles_mplus for some options you can contro
  • The functions that use mclust (those that don’t end in _mplus) are initialized by a hierarchical cluster analysis, so there’s only one set of start values (those that are the end-values/estimates from the hierarchical cluster analysis)

HTH!

Josh

parts:
Thank you so much.  I appreciate your responses and your software.

One more thing.   I was running some bootstrap likellihood tests (without accessing Mplus).   Twice, I had trouble (though several times things worked well).   The first problem simply stalled: 

> bootstrap_lrt(d, 
+               Q2, Q4, Q5, Q6, Q7, Q8, Q9, Q10, 
+               model = 3)
Note. This function is still in-development and may cause unexpected errors.
bootstrapping LRTS ...
  |=======================                                                        |  29%

The second problem seemingly couldn't access mclust.

> bootstrap_lrt(d, 
+               Q2, Q4, Q5, Q6, Q7, Q8, Q9, Q10, 
+               model = 6)
Note. This function is still in-development and may cause unexpected errors.
Error in bootstrap_lrt(d, Q2, Q4, Q5, Q6, Q7, Q8, Q9, Q10, model = 6) : 
  Model name is not correctly specified: use 1, 2, or 3 (see ?estimate_profiles for descriptions) or one of the model names specified from mclustModelNames() from mclust

I used mclust syntax and then it stalled again in computing the three class solution:  

library(mclust)
trial = mclustBootstrapLRT(d, model = "VVV")
trial

I let these run for about 20 minutes each before stopping them.  I'm wondering if you think these will eventually converge or if these will just hang indefinitely.

Thanks,
Steve

Steven, I sincerely apologie for my delay – thanks for asking. Short answer: I’m not sure. This function is pretty much a wrapper around the mclust function MclustBootstrap(). If you can, I’d be curious to see what happens after letting it run for awhile…

 

If that doesn’t work, you (I’d be happy to, too) could also reach out to the mclust folks (see their names here: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/27818791).

I’m sorry again for the delay and I’m sorry I couldn’t be more helpful!

Josh
